messages:
sophia: quick heads-up — ACME reported a sudden p99 jump on hosted /v1/generate yesterday evening, latency went from ~1.2s to ~12s; customer is impacted and asking for immediate mitigation. Looks like GPU memory pressure + allocator slowpaths. Logs: ```gpu_mem=98% slow_alloc_ms=84 evict_ops=1.2k/min prefix_cache_size=1.9GB``` Can eng take a look?

deploy-bot: rollout completed: model=x-v2 pool=sea-gpu-3 at 2026-03-15T21:12Z
devin: on it. do you have tenant id, route, and a sample request? also which pool / capacity were they hitting?
sophia: tenant=ACME-42, route=/v1/generate, sample prompt hash=0x8f3a, pool=sea-gpu-3. Customer sent curl sample (trimmed): ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -d '{"prompt":"<long conversation>"}'```
mike: quick read — hypothesis: v2 increased on-GPU prefix cache footprint and introduces heavier allocation churn during KV inserts -> fragmentation + slow allocation path (observed slow_alloc). Repro able with synthetic batch + prefix cache churn on sea-gpu-3 dev pool.
anya: recommended short-term mitigations: 1) add per-route concurrency cap for ACME (soft throttle) 2) increase reserved capacity for their pool (burst) 3) revert to x-v1 if needed. I can apply throttle now if support confirms.
sophia: please apply throttle, customer is breathing down our neck. Also please share rollback steps so I can coord with CS.
devin: applying soft limit: adding routing policy header X-Route-Max-Concurrency=2 for tenant ACME-42 on /v1/generate. Command: ```redwoodctl routing set --tenant ACME-42 --route /v1/generate --max-concurrency 2 --soft``` Doing it now.
anya: I also scaled the pool by +1 reserved GPU while we triage: ```redwoodctl clusters scale --pool=sea-gpu-3 --reserve +1```
leah: told ACME CS will throttle requests and we're looking at rollback if that doesn't help. Asked for ETA within 15 minutes.
devin: throttle is live. monitoring logs/metrics. initial telemetry: p99 dropped from 12s -> 3.6s within 30s but still above baseline.
mike: ok trying quick revert of model variant to x-v1 on a small canary for tenant only: ```redwoodctl rollout set --tenant ACME-42 --route /v1/generate --model x-v1 --force-canary 10%``` If that looks good we'll do immediate full revert.
sophia: ACME asked for full rollback if canary is successful.
devin: canary shows p99 ~1.3s after 3m, memory footprint on the worker dropped ~30%. Proceeding to full revert. ```redwoodctl rollout set --route /v1/generate --model x-v1 --force```
mike: after full revert: sea-gpu-3 worker mem usage down 28%, slow_alloc_ms dropped to ~6ms, evict_ops down to ~120/min. p99 back to ~1.2s — marking this mitigation successful. :thumbsup:
sophia: passing update to ACME: full rollback done, latency back near baseline, monitoring for 1h then we'll follow up. They appreciated quick action.
leah: noted customer is satisfied for now but asked for a postmortem + prevention plan.
devin: next actions (short list): 1) open ENG-RUNTIME-2318 with reproducer + heap/alloc hist 2) experiment with allocator flags (reduce arenas / tune jemalloc) 3) lower default prefix cache threshold and add eviction hysteresis for model variants that increase footprint 4) add automated alert for slow_alloc_ms > 20ms. I opened ticket ENG-RUNTIME-2318 and attached traces.
mike: also adding hotspot: ensure background compaction/defrag runs more aggressively during heavy KV churn; may need allocator-level defrag. I'll sketch a safe rollout plan.
anya: oncall notes: if we see similar spike again, immediate steps = apply soft throttle -> scale pool -> rollback model variant -> investigate traces. Make runbook snippet.
sophia: thanks everyone — closing here after follow-ups created. Will set a quick sync with CS + eng-runtime tomorrow.
devin: filing PR with safe eviction defaults and adding a metric dashboard (PR#4512).
mike: filing infra task to test allocator config matrix on staging (task#INF-907).
sophia: leaving this thread open until postmortem links posted in ENG-RUNTIME-2318.
